explanation: The selected plan treats missing Stop callbacks and stale shared app-server state as vendor concerns, but the owner included issue 174. The repository also drops prompt-less Stop events when multiple issues remain active, or routes an unknown session to a sole unrelated issue; stale COORD_ISSUE precedes prompt identity. Pane recovery alone leaves those original failures intact. Add session-correlated hook routing and isolated Codex launch using the installed CLI-supported --no-daemon flag, with focused regression tests in existing files. Keep the selected delivery recovery and its composer/race corrections within the already approved files; do not fabricate idle events, relax sandbox grants, or terminate a shared daemon.

additionalPaths.reason: This owns issue resolution for lifecycle callbacks. Resolve prompt-less callbacks through an unambiguous existing session binding, validate explicit/environment identities against prompt and session evidence, and reject ambiguous or unrelated fallback routing so a real Stop reaches its own issue without updating another issue.

Extend the existing runtime fixture to reproduce a prompt-bound Codex session with a Stop lacking issue environment while another issue remains active. Cover stale environment, ambiguous session matches and an unknown session with a sole unrelated active issue, asserting no cross-issue lifecycle mutation.

This is the canonical generated Codex launcher. Add --no-daemon to avoid attaching the new issue to a shared server with stale issue environment or an incompatible CLI version, as reported in issue 174. Preserve the existing approval policy, workspace-write sandbox and exact per-issue grants; do not kill shared processes.

Extend existing generated-launcher execution tests to assert Codex receives --no-daemon while retaining its current issue environment, sandbox and narrowly scoped grants, including manual launch. This verifies the actual shell argv instead of merely matching template text.
